findings: All incorrect component triplets combine several unrelated sensing/gearing/bearing functions. Replace at least the torque-sensor/speed-reducer and stationary-encoder/bearing alternatives with credible stator-versus-rotor, brush-versus-commutator, or encoder-versus-current-switching role confusions. The correct roles and preserved ironless-winding qualification are sound.

Converting encoder angle into a gear ratio and eliminating every magnetic field are not plausible commutator purposes. Use competing electrical/mechanical misconceptions, such as maintaining current magnitude independent of speed or confusing mechanical commutation with electronic speed measurement, while preserving the chosen supply-polarity condition.

Numerical equality of velocity and magnetic-field magnitudes compares unlike units, and negative charge making every force zero is a weak competitor. Use physically meaningful angle/direction alternatives or a concrete cross-product scenario with distinct plausible outcomes.

The supplied arithmetic is correct, but describing one motor with k_m=0.4 N·m/A and k_e=0.2 V/(rad/s) is not physically consistent with the conventional ideal SI electromechanical conversion model. At the stated i=3 A and speed=10 rad/s, electromagnetic mechanical power k_m i ω=12 W exceeds back-EMF conversion power k_e ω i=6 W. Use a consistent common SI constant, or explicitly frame this as two independent algebraic relations rather than a physically specified ideal motor; update all affected values if changed.

The alternative that increased motor speed changes only the fixed gear ratio is unrelated to the electrical question. Replace it with a credible current-slew or voltage-drop misconception; the two existing opposing-sign/current-dependence distractors are useful.

A motor-position jump and a torque constant becoming zero are not credible rivals to current continuity. Replace them with plausible confusion between current, current derivative, inductive voltage and instantaneous current tracking.
This directly restates the source’s nonzero-inductance current-continuity consequence. Mark easy unless the revision adds a substantive transient or impulse calculation.

The assertion that nonzero inductance makes its effect exactly zero is internally unmotivated. Replace it and the driver-speed distractor with concrete competing time-scale assumptions, such as electrical response comparable to or slower than the mechanical dynamics. Keep the physically meaningful fast-current-loop premise.
